canonical_statement: The study aimed to investigate dyspnea sensation in hypoxemic emergency admissions.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The aim of this study was to investigate the sensation of dyspnea in hypoxemic emergency admissions.

canonical_statement: All emergency admissions to the Siloah Hospital respiratory care unit from October 1 to November 1, 2020 were analyzed retrospectively.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: All emergency admissions to the respiratory care unit ... between October 1 and November 1, 2020, were analyzed retrospectively.

canonical_statement: Patients were included when supplementary oxygen was required within 24 hours of admission to achieve SpO2 >=92%.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Patients with hypoxemia defined as supplementary oxygen demand to achieve an oxygen saturation (SpO2) >= 92% in the first 24 h after admission were included.

population.label: Eligible hypoxemic admissions
inclusion_criteria: Supplementary oxygen demand to achieve SpO2 >=92% in first 24 h after admission

canonical_statement: All patients received SARS-CoV-2 PCR testing on admission.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: SARS-CoV-2 PCR testing on admission.

canonical_statement: Vital signs were monitored with NEWS-2, and oxygen demand was titrated using capillary blood gas analysis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Vital signs were recorded, and the national early warning score (NEWS-2) was used for monitoring. Oxygen demand was titrated by capillary blood gas analysis.

canonical_statement: Perceived dyspnea was measured using the modified Borg CR10 scale, which the article describes as 12 stages from 0 to 10 including 0.5.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Subjects rated their perceived dyspnea using the modified Borg CR10 scale ... This scale has 12 stages from 0 to 10 including 0.5.

outcome.definition: Patient-rated perceived dyspnea on modified Borg CR10 scale

canonical_statement: Continuous variables were summarized as medians with 25th and 75th percentiles; categorical variables as n (%); categorical comparisons used chi-square or Fisher exact tests, and metric comparisons used Student tests after normality testing.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Continuous variables were described as median and 25 and 75% quartiles. Categorical variables are presented as n (%).

canonical_statement: The logistic regression used Borg CR10 >=5 as the categorical outcome and included variables with univariate p<0.1.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A logistic regression model was fitted with a Borg CR10 scale of >=5 as the categorical outcome. Variables included were identified by a p value of <0.1 in univariate analysis.

canonical_statement: The study included 82 patients: 45 (55%) with SARS-CoV-2 detected by PCR and 37 (45%) without COVID-19.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: During the study period, 82 patients were included. In 45/82 (55%) patients, SARS-CoV-2 was detected by PCR on admission.

canonical_statement: The narrative/abstract reports an OR of 0.221 (95% CI 0.054-0.907, p=0.036) for “silent hypoxemia” associated with COVID-19 and severe hypocapnia, but this estimate is not directly represented in Table 2 as printed.

canonical_statement: The article inconsistently labels Borg CR10 >=5 as “silent hypoxemia” in narrative text while Table 2 labels Borg >=5 as dyspnea; the direction conflicts with the concept of less dyspnea.

canonical_statement: The Discussion states that COVID-19 patients had a “higher dyspnea sensation,” which conflicts with the abstract, Results, and Figure 1 showing lower Borg ratings in COVID-19.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Patients with COVID-19 had a higher dyspnea sensation as assessed by the BORG scale when the oxygen partial pressure was similar.

canonical_statement: The authors identify the single-center design, small sample size, and resulting lack of subgroup analysis as limitations.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The series has potential limitation from the unicenter design with a small number of participants and a following lack of subgroup analysis.

canonical_statement: SARS-CoV-2 variants were not screened in clinical routine during the study period.

canonical_statement: The authors note that the Borg CR10 scale is designed for dyspnea during physical work and is not established for rating dyspnea at rest in acute hypoxemia.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The Borg CR10 scale is a tool for measuring an individual’s dyspnea during physical work. The scale is not established to rate dyspnea in patients with acute hypoxemia at rest.

canonical_statement: The authors conclude that silent hypoxemia is more common in COVID-19 patients than in pulmonary patients with acute hypoxemia and that further study of its uniqueness and mechanisms is needed.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Silent hypoxemia is more common in COVID-19 patients compared to pulmonary patients with acute hypoxemia. Further evaluation of its uniqueness and pathophysiologic mechanisms is needed.
